newsitem.title: USA: US blue chips lower after data but techs positive.
newsitem.headline: US blue chips lower after data but techs positive.

text.p: U.S. stocks took a tumble after reports of high consumer confidence and strength in new home sales startled the financial markets, with blue chips off their session lows but still weak in quiet midday trading'.
The Dow Industrials were off about 16 to 6533 after slowly climbing off a 30-point deficit sparked after the release of the data. Bonds and the Standard & Poor's 500 were also lower.
But technology stocks bucked the trend and posted slight gains in a rebound from yesterday's losses. The Nasdaq Composite Index rose two to nearly 1290.

"The consumer confidence numbers and the housing numbers were materially stronger than the Street had anticipated ... so this is a knee-jerk reaction by bonds and stocks," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management division.

The Conference Board reported U.S. consumer confidence rose sharply in December to 113.8 versus a revised 109.5 in November. At the same time, November new home sales blew out economists' expectations and jumped 14.2 pct to 772,000, the steepest rise since April 1993.
The long bond fell over a point in the wake of the data.
The Chicago Purchasing Management Index for December was also stronger than expected, coming in at 57.4 compared to 57.6 last month and beating expectations for a reading of about 55.6.

Orlando said investors might be jittery for a few days after the robust data, awaiting more evidence on the direction of the economy. Wall Street is currently comfortable with its forecasts for a gradual slowing of the economy with no danger of any rise in interest rates.

Technology stocks rebounded slightly after yesterday's losses. Compaq Computer Corp rose 1-1/8 to 74-7/8 and Dell Computer Corp added 1-7/8 to 54-1/8 after NatWest Securities raised its earnings forecasts for the companies.

"Millenium" software companies, which address data problems when computers switch into the year 2000, also rebounded from yesterday's steep losses. Zitel Corp rose 4-5/8 to 45-5/8 and Accelr8 Technology moved up 2-1/8 to 18-1/2.
Service Merchandise Co Inc lost 3/8 to 4-1/8 and hit a new low for the year of 3-7/8 after it forecast lower fourth quarter same-store sales.

Iomega Corp shares lost 1/2 to 16 in heavy trading and hit a new low of 15-1/2. The maker of the Jaz and Zip disk drives said it will take a $10 million pretax charge in the fourth quarter to shift more of its production to Asia, cutting up to 700 jobs at its Roy, Utah, facility.
Associated Estates Realty Corp rose after Standard & Poor's said the outlook for the real estate investment trust turned positive from stable. Shares rose 1/4 to 23-3/8.
